# Abstract {.unnumbered}

<!-- Max 150 words (master's) or 350 words (doctoral). Same line spacing as the body.
     Keywords come from `keywords` in _quarto.yml and are added after the abstract. -->

This thesis evaluates public policies with difference-in-differences methods. The
first essay studies the effect of a wage increase for recruits of the Night's Watch on
enlistment at Castle Black, using Eastwatch-by-the-Sea as a comparison garrison.
Following the design of Card and Krueger's minimum wage study, I find no decline in
enlistment after the wage increase. The thesis discusses the parallel trends assumption
and its implications for policy evaluation in the Seven Kingdoms.
